headline: The product is right; the gate is not closed. I verified both of the founder's complaints as actually fixed on the LIVE deploy — and the mandatory evidence still binds to f26a2c1 with verdict FAIL. On the exact round that proved a confident claim can ship a no-op, I will not waive the gate that caught it.

why_iterate_anyway: My own live check is one instrument, run by the party who wants the ACCEPT. It is additional evidence, never a substitute for the gate. CLAUDE.md §3 makes Reviewer ≥ 8/10 and a PASSing delivery-evidence gate mandatory for UI/flow work, and I hold no waiver authority over either. Right now .orbit/qa/delivery-evidence.json is bound to f26a2c1 with verdict FAIL — 4 failed scenarios, a failed dependency regression, and three #kmon/22 pixel comparisons at 34.31% / 25.99% / 4.54%. The delivery-quality-gate at 67dc8ff returns status BLOCKED. An ACCEPT written over a BLOCKED gate is exactly the shape of the defect this round exposed: a claim asserted rather than measured. Re-running is cheap; the fix is done and deployed, so this is evidence work, not build work.
reviewer_qa_question_answered: BOTH must be re-run against 67dc8ff — my live verification does not substitute. Reviewer's 4/10 and QA's BLOCK were scored on f26a2c1, a commit whose defining property was that its stated fix did not execute; they carry no signal about 67dc8ff in either direction. The pixel diffs are the sharper reason: 34% at 375x812 is the campaign board's numbers changing from fabricated to true, which is the INTENDED change — but 'intended' is a claim, and a re-baseline is how it becomes a measurement. Scope: re-score the 67dc8ff diff only, re-bind evidence, re-baseline #kmon/22 at all three viewports with the delta explained. Not a redo of the work.

The opposite of slop is present — check-campaign-scope.mjs prints its own honest warning that a gate asserting with an invented ISO string is how the no-op shipped clean. A guard that names its own failure mode is the anti-slop signal.

user_model_update.durable_lesson: A fix is unproven until it has run against the shape the SOURCE returns, not the shape the fixture assumes. f26a2c1 was correct TypeScript, passed tsc, passed review-by-reading, and did nothing — because created_at is BIGINT and node-pg hands int8 back as a digit string, so Date.parse gave NaN and the window collapsed to 0, the maximally permissive value. The invented ISO fixture agreed with the code and both were wrong together. Two rules follow: (1) any fix that reads a value crossing a boundary must be tested against a sample captured FROM that boundary — for DB reads, log the raw value and its typeof once before writing the parser; (2) a parse fallback on a truth surface must fail CLOSED. Returning 0 for 'I could not read the launch time' meant 'show everything' — the failure defaulted to the exact lie being fixed. Infinity (show nothing) is the only honest default on a screen whose whole job is to not overclaim.
user_model_update.signal_class: engineering discipline (system-level), not a user-preference claim — derived from the founder's own two complaints and the measured no-op, not invented.
